transformations.name: De-tensorize
transformations.statement: Replace an invariant that composes badly under products with one that composes correctly.
transformations.diagnostic: Stated in the seed only informally.

seed_evidence.note: On cases 2 and 3 the needed move runs the opposite way: progress required an invariant that is MULTIPLICATIVE, because the target itself is (super)multiplicative. Case 1 changes the product law from additive to Pythagorean.

transformations.name: Collectivize a union bound
transformations.statement: Replace a union bound over m bad events with a single collective argument.
transformations.diagnostic: A union bound over m events appears in the composition slot.

seed_evidence.note: Candidate refinement, UNTESTED: ask whether some instance in the class makes the m bad events near-independent. If it does, the log is real.

transformations.name: Auxiliary-witness lift
transformations.statement: Introduce an auxiliary object whose existence certifies the bound.
transformations.seed_verdict: NO STATED DIAGNOSTIC; NEAR-ZERO DISCRIMINATING POWER

seed_evidence.note: Fits almost anything post hoc. This is the programme's own E9 criticism applied to the programme.
Only case 2 fits, and only weakly - it abolishes the iteration entirely.

candidate_replacements.statement: Compute how the target behaves on the product construction of the extremal family, and require the invariant to obey the same law.
candidate_replacements.relation: E4 becomes the special case where the target is flat.
candidate_replacements.fatal_caveat: Derived from the same cases it was then scored on. It needs cases chosen by someone who has not seen the hypothesis. Until then it is a guess.

label_vocabulary.none_means: The historical change fits no entry in the catalogue.
label_vocabulary.unlabelled_means: The seed's preliminary scoring assigned no label. Not the same as 'none'.

dropped_criteria.dropped: no metric for 'cheaper' is stated, so it is not computable from the before-board. Same standard as auxiliary-witness lift. See D9-ADJUDICATION.md.

level_axis.what_this_is: AN AXIS, NOT A TRANSFORMATION. Debt D30 asked for the level and substrate of a change to be encoded, and explicitly forbade adding a sixth transformation: the standing rule is that catalogues shrink before they grow. The transformation vocabulary is unchanged and stays closed; this is a separate field answering a separate question -- WHERE in the stack the change happened, not what kind of change it was.
level_axis.why_it_exists: Control 16 (Zhang) is only a valid control with the level stated. He left the GPY sieve untouched and improved what it consumes, raising the level of distribution past 1/2 for smooth moduli. Without the axis, 'the board did not change' and 'a board one level down did change' are the same sentence, and the control is mislabelled.

values.same-level: The bound stays on the same object and that object's own board changed -- its state, move, invariant or terminal certificate.
values.input-level: The board whose bound is at issue is left INTACT, and something it CONSUMES changed. Zhang: the sieve is GPY's, the equidistribution input is not.
values.reduction-level: The bound is moved onto a DIFFERENT OBJECT by a reduction, and the old board is retired rather than consumed. Elekes-Sharir sending distances to rigid motions to lines in R^3; the neighbourhood complex sending a colouring problem to topology.
values.substrate: The same mechanism re-expressed in a different substrate, where whether it is one board or two is CONTESTED by the practitioners rather than by us.
values.unclear: DELIBERATELY UNUSED AT PRESENT. It exists so that a later encoder is not forced to choose, because a forced label is what produced kappa = 0.048 on the transformation vocabulary. Using it is not a failure; forcing a call would be.

level_axis.boundary_that_is_weakest: same-level versus reduction-level. 'A new invariant on the same object' and 'a reduction to a new object' shade into each other -- cases 6 and 11 are assigned reduction-level at MEDIUM confidence and are the first two items a second encoder should be asked about.
level_axis.status: SINGLE-ENCODER AND UNVALIDATED, exactly like the v0 transformation labels. No second encoder has assigned these. The one reason to expect better than kappa = 0.048 is D20's split result: closed-vocabulary FIELDS reproduced at +0.811 and +0.755 while the RULE built on them did not, and this is a field. That is a reason for optimism, not evidence.
level_axis.how_to_test_it: The same instrument as D20: tools/make_rating_sheet.py over the 17 scoreable items, raters who have not seen this file, Fleiss kappa against the 0.048 baseline. It is a one-field sheet, so it is cheaper than D20 was.
